name: Aduro Clean Technologies Inc.
blurb: Aduro Clean Technologies is a small-cap Canadian cleantech company (founded 2011, ~25 employees) that develops water-based chemical recycling processes under its proprietary Hydrochemolytic Technology (HCT) platform. Its core applications span three verticals: converting end-of-life plastics and tire rubber into specialty chemicals and fuels, upgrading heavy crude oils and bitumen, and transforming renewable oils into renewable fuels and specialty chemicals. The company operates at near-zero commercial revenue (trailing twelve-month revenue of ~$177K), positioning it as a pre-commercial technology licensor rather than a manufacturer. It was formerly known as Dimension Five Technologies.
recent: As of mid-May 2026, ADUR trades around $12.75 (down ~3.8% on May 13), well below its 52-week high of $17.66 but up sharply from the $5.88 low, with a market cap of roughly $430M reflecting speculative growth expectations rather than current earnings. The company reported Q results on April 15, 2026; with a net loss of $13.3M and minimal revenue, the stock remains unprofitable. Sell-side analysts carry a consensus Strong Buy with an average price target of $38.67, implying more than 200% upside, though the analyst base is small given the company's micro-cap profile.
